title: Oncall evidence extraction + priority matrix
body:
Purpose:
Quick reference for oncall responders to extract relevant evidence from the SIEM, map audit-log fields (RBAC v2 aware), and package artifacts for incident tickets and postmortems. Focus is: fast, reproducible, and auditable extraction that plays nicely with our evidence automation flows.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to suspicious authz/access events, privilege escalations, anomalous service account activity, suspicious data egress patterns.
- SIEM: primarily Splunk but includes ELK snippets where relevant.
- Audit logs follow the RBAC v2 audit schema (see mapping below).
- This is a working doc: expect shorthand, quick queries, TODO flags.

Triage priority matrix (oncall quick view):
- P0 (Blocker) = confirmed active compromise / ongoing exfil / service outage caused by security incident. Immediate pager, Exec notify.
- P1 (High) = confirmed unauthorized access to production resources, high-risk token compromise. Page security lead and SRE.
- P2 (Medium) = suspicious but unconfirmed activity, failed escalations, repeated anomalous reads. Create incident ticket, monitor.
- P3 (Low) = informational, potential policy gaps, baseline anomalies. Track, no page.

Key indicators to escalate to P0/P1:
- Any CREATE/ASSUME_ROLE/GRANT_ROLE where the actor is unexpected AND occurs outside maintenance windows.
- High-volume read/download from data stores by a single principal in <30m.
- New keys created for long-lived service accounts and immediate use.
- Cross-region data transfers flagged as unusual by cost/traffic baselines.

RBAC v2 audit-log schema (canonical mapping) - fields to prioritize when exporting evidence:
- ts (timestamp) -> event_time (ISO8601)
- actor_id -> user_id / principal_id (normalize service vs human)
- actor_role -> actor_roles (list)
- action -> verb (e.g., iam.grant, sessions.create, queries.execute)
- target_resource -> resource_id
- resource_type -> resource_kind (cluster, model, dataset, secret, route)
- outcome -> result (success|failure|denied)
- request_id -> request_id (correlate with gateway traces)
- trace_id -> trace_id (link to APM spans)
- raw_payload -> raw_event (base64 if large)
- auth_context -> mfa_used / origin_ip / user_agent
Notes: ensure event_time is normalized to UTC in all exports and we include original event raw_payload for forensic parsing.

Essential SIEM extraction queries (Splunk primary):
- Find privilege changes in last 30m:
  index=redwood_audit source=audit_logs action=iam.grant OR action=iam.revoke | table _time, actor_id, action, target_resource, outcome, request_id

- Large reads from prod dataset (top principals):
  index=redwood_telemetry source=data_access earliest=-1h host=prod* | stats sum(bytes_read) as bytes by principal | sort -bytes | head 30

- New long-lived key creation + immediate usage (fingerprint):
  index=redwood_audit action=keys.create OR action=keys.activate | eval created_ts=_time | join request_id [ search index=redwood_audit action=keys.use ] | table _time, actor_id, key_id, request_id, target_resource

ELK (Elasticsearch) snippet for ad-hoc export:
- POST /_search?pretty
  { "query": { "bool": { "must": [{ "match": { "action": "iam.grant" }}, { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "now-1h" }}}]}}

Evidence collection steps (oncall checklist):
1) Capture context in ticket: short summary, observed indicator (IP, user, request_id), time window, severity estimate.
2) Run targeted SIEM queries (use above snippets). Save raw results as JSON and CSV.
3) Pull correlated traces: request_id -> APM trace (zipkin/jaeger) and gateway logs.
4) Export audit log slices with full raw_payload for the window +/- 15m around the key event.
5) Snapshot RBAC state for involved principals: group memberships, active roles, attached policies.
6) Hash and store evidence artifacts in evidence-bucket (S3 path pattern: s3://redwood-evidence/{incident_id}/{artifact}.sha256).
7) Mark chain-of-custody in the ticket (who pulled, when, note if private keys/PHI present).
8) Trigger automation (if P0/P1): run evidence-collection lambda: /infra/playbooks/collect-evidence (see linked PR).

Packaging for SIEM export and handoff:
- Attachments: raw_audit_slice.json, siem_query_result.csv, apm_trace_{id}.json, rbac_snapshot.json, host_forensics_{host}.tar.gz (if host access).
- Metadata (ticket fields): incident_id, primary_indicator, initial_alert_source, time_window, exported_by, export_checksum.
- For legal path: flag evidence with legal_hold=true and notify compliance@redwood.ai.

Automation hooks & quick commands:
- Kick the evidence-collector lambda (requires infra-run role): aws lambda invoke --function-name collect-evidence --payload '{"incident_id":"INC-1234","start":"2024-12-01T12:00:00Z","end":"2024-12-01T12:20:00Z"}' /tmp/out.json
- Splunk export to S3 using savedsearch: splunk search """| savedsearch "incident_extract_INC-1234""" | outputcsv /tmp/inc-1234.csv && aws s3 cp /tmp/inc-1234.csv s3://redwood-evidence/INC-1234/inc-1234.csv
- Generate RBAC snapshot (ad-hoc): python tools/rbac_snapshot.py --principals user:alice,svc:batch --out rbac_snapshot_inc1234.json

Chain-of-custody minimum fields to record in ticket:
- extractor_name, extractor_email, extraction_command, extraction_time, artifact_path, sha256_checksum, notes_on_serialization

Comms templates (short):
- Pager: "SEC PAGER: possible privilege escalation detected for principal {principal} on {resource} at {time}. Query results attached. Please acknowledge and triage."
- L2 handoff: include incident_id, current evidence S3 path, suspected impact, next steps (isolate principal, rotate keys, revoke session tokens).

Post-incident artifacts required for postmortem (to attach before closing):
- Exported SIEM slices (raw), RBAC snapshots, APM traces, remediation timeline, list of rotated keys and who approved, affected customer IDs (if any), SLA/uptime impact notes, estimated cost impact (if infrastructure mitigations were invoked).

Postmortem quick template (to copy into incident ticket):
- Title: [INC-XXXX] short summary
- Severity: P0/P1/P2/P3
- Timeline: bullet list ISO8601 times + actor/ids
- Root cause hypothesis: short
- Mitigation & remediation: what changed (rotations, ACL updates, playbook updates)
- Action items: owner + ETA + verification steps
- Evidence archive path & checksums

Common pitfalls / notes-to-self:
- Don’t drop PII into public Slack; use private #sec-ops for attachments.
- When in doubt capture more context than less; we can filter later but missing raw_payload is painful.
- RBAC snapshots should include pending/in-flight grants (check iam.audit:event_reason).
- Watch for clock skew between services; prefer request_id correlation over exact timestamps when possible.

Run example (anonymized):
- 2024-09-18T03:21Z alert: anomaly-detector flagged large read from dataset-prod by svc-reporting-42. Query run returned 1.2TB transferred in 12m.
- Action: P1 assigned. Extracted SIEM slice +/- 15m, pulled APM trace for request_id=req-9f3e. RBAC snapshot showed svc-reporting-42 had unexpected role attach 6m prior (iam.grant by user jdoe).
- Mitigation: rotated keys for svc-reporting-42, revoked active sessions, opened request to infra to revoke temporary tokens, legal notified. Evidence archived s3://redwood-evidence/INC-20240918-01.

Open questions / TODO:
- Add automations for ELK -> S3 export that preserve original event_time zone metadata (ticketed: JIRA-SEC-4199).
- Consider adding a single-click "snapshot all RBAC for incident" in Console (product request).
- Validate that evidence-collector lambda logs PII redaction status automatically.

Contacts & escalation path:
- primary oncall (security): @sec-oncall (Pager duty)
- security lead: Samir Patel (samir@redwood.ai)
- SRE oncall: #sre-oncall Slack
- legal & compliance: compliance@redwood.ai

Last notes:
- This is a living runbook. If you add or change a query, paste it into the linked PR and add a test case. Keep things minimal on the pager path — prefer page escalation only for P0/P1.

-- Avery (notes: Will follow-up to add savedsearch names and sample outputs; check with Samir about evidence retention policy update in Q1)
